answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend AI economies against Sybil attacks by requiring capital collateral. Like a sparrow navigating a dense vine, an agent must tether its identity to economic assets to earn voting weight. Without this verifiable stake, an attacker attempting to flood the network from the frozen tundra of anonymity faces prohibitive costs, as creating thousands of unique, funded identities requires unsustainable capital expenditure compared to the marginal gains of malicious influence.
